And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#2069. Major Sheffield Wednesday v Plymouth Argyle flashpoint causes big online stir

Sheffield Wednesday fans went home happy on Saturday, as they cruised to a comfortable 3-0 win over fellow promotion-chasing side, Plymouth Argyle.

It was the perfect start to life in charge of the Owls in League One for Dave Challinor, who picked up three points at the first available opportunity in front of the Owls supporters.

Billy Mitchell opened the scoring on the day for Sheffield Wednesday, which came just before the half-time whistle. Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard then added two late goals to secure an eye-catching win at Hillsborough.

Bernard's goal late on was the pick of the bunch, as he fired home in emphatic style from distance, much to the surprise and delight of the home crowd.

The result means that Sheffield Wednesday moved ahead of Plymouth in the table, and up to fifth, as they look to finish in the top-six in League One this term.

One of the main talking points from the win over Tom Cleverley's side wasn't any of the goals on the day though, as a poor challenge from Plymouth's Ronan Curtis only saw a yellow card awarded to the winger.

Ronan Curtis' challenge on Jamal Lowe was at chest height, and the Hillsborough crowd were left furious that only a yellow card was awarded, with many feeling as though there wasn't any other option than a red card.

Lowe was able to carry on and play on, before being substituted for Liam Palmer with five minutes remaining in the match, and he'll be hoping he can kick on and feature for the Owls in their bid for promotion.

Curtis didn't appear to be looking at Lowe beforehand, and some Plymouth fans came to their player's defence for the incident which sparked plenty of debate on social media.

The Plymouth winger was apologetic after it occurred, but it certainly endangered Lowe with his boot being so high off the ground, and so there was real surprise to only see a yellow card shown by the referee.

Do you think it should have been a no-brainer for Curtis' challenge to be worthy of a red card instead of a yellow?

Speaking to The Star after the win over Plymouth, newly-appointed Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor issued his verdict on the challenge from Curtis, and felt as though it was right to appeal for a red card.

"Well, it's definitely chest high. I think you're always going to appeal for it. I think Tom (Cleverley) would have been appealing for it exactly the same, and he was open to that. What do you need to do? What constitutes a red card? If it catches him on the jaw, did Ronan Curtis mean it? I'd probably suggest no."

The ball's coming over his shoulder, but if one of our players would have done that, I would have been fearing the worst. Thankfully, it didn't make a huge impact at the end of the game."

"He (referee) said there was, I think, minimal force. I suggest if it's you on the end of it, it might have a different thought. It's high. It's probably one of them ones you toss a coin, 50% of referees flash a red without even thinking."

#2068. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2067. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2066. Fresh £30m-40m claim made on Birmingham City ace Jay Stansfield

A fresh claim has been made over the importance of Jay Stansfield to Chris Davies' Birmingham City side, with the club's record signing currently enjoying a strong patch of form.

The 23-year-old's time at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park has garnered plenty of attention ever since he was lured back to the club two summers ago for an eye-catching fee in excess of £15m from Premier League side, Fulham, on a seven-year contract.

Stansfield has since become the 'poster boy' of Knighthead Capital Management's ambitious rebuild in this part of the world, and that has brought its own advantages and pressures.

After recently surpassing 150 appearances in royal blue, the England youth international striker's brace against Swansea City last Saturday was enough to see him become the latest player to have scored 50 goals in all competitions for the club and send Davies' side top of the Championship.

Stansfield's current form is a stark contrast to the frustrations which he endured last term whilst adapting to a new role within Davies' setup, and with that being said, Football League World quizzed our Birmingham City fan pundit, Jason Moore, if the attacker is deemed 'untouchable' in January.

Stansfield was one of two Birmingham players who reached double-figures last season, albeit two of his 11 goals came after the turn of the year, leaving question marks over his performance levels and output.

It was then claimed in the summer that the forward was the subject of interest from clubs such as Everton, Hull City, Ipswich Town and Sunderland, with Stansfield's reported valuation coming in at the £25m mark as a result.

Oliver Glasner's side are reportedly interested in acquiring Phil Neumann from the Championship leaders

The forward later reaffirmed his commitment to the cause at St. Andrew's, although it was widely debated whether Birmingham should have potentially considered moving on their prized asset for said price.

Birmingham have seen goals fly in from all angles so far this season, with Davies' tactical reshuffles certainly getting the best out of Patrick Roberts, Liam Millar, Stansfield and August Priske in recent weeks.

Priske has netted six goals so far this season, but his absence in the victories over Millwall and Swansea allowed Stansfield to return to the main striking role, scoring three times in 180 minutes' worth of action, taking his seasonal tally to four strikes and one assist.

As such, Moore believes that even more would need to be coughed up if suitors were to even attempt prizing him away from B9.

"I got asked the same question in the August transfer window and back then I said 'take what you can get for him, go and reinvest in the squad', but I just can't do it," he told FLW.

"He's 'Blues', he gets what we're about, and I don't think you'll find a Blues fan that's got a bad word to say about him now. I was calling to probably sell him, but no, keep him. He is 'Mr Birmingham' at the moment.

Blues fans, how do you rate Jay Stansfield's season so far /10? Comment below!

"He's not scoring goals, but he just works so hard for the team, and he's literally just what we're about," Moore added.

"He's pivotal to what Chris Davies is doing with the way we're playing. So no, and I know I'm going to sound ridiculous here, but unless you're giving us like £30-40m no, I don't want him gone.

"You might get some fans who say 'that's silly, take £20m', not for me. I love him so much, I'd rather just find the money another way and keep him."

Stansfield's importance to Blues right now is way beyond his goalscoring exploits, even though some would still expect a strong return given his price tag.

Emphasising such a viewpoint, Davies recently said of the forward: "As a manager, you always go with the ones that you know are going to give everything, and one thing with him is, he gives absolutely everything in every game."

#2065. The 3 summer targets West Ham should pursue again in January, including a new Arne Engels midfield partner

West Ham currently sit 9th in the Championship table following the sacking of Nuno Espirito Santo and hiring of Scott Parker. WHUFC will hope the three-time promotion-winning boss can deliver the same success after his spells at Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham.

However, the squad also needs refreshing when the January transfer window comes around. The defence has been heavily criticised and is sure to be an area targeted for reinforcements by the Hammers.

New targets will be on the radar, but West Ham identified some smart options in the summer who could be available this winter. Here, we put forward three summer transfer targets who should be back on their radar ahead of January…

For all of West Ham’s attacking success this season, their defence has been a concern. Konstantinos Mavropanos has chipped in with five goals as a set-piece threat, but defensively, he and Max Kilman have left a lot to be desired.

Mavropanos is the subject of persisting interest from the likes of Besiktas. A new centre-back may be needed regardless of what comes of the Greek defender’s situation, and Axel Disasi should be on the radar.

Disasi has endured a tough start to life at Crystal Palace and rumours are circulating about an early departure from the Premier League. Should he do so, a return to WHUFC could benefit all parties.

West Ham have endured uncertainty in midfield for a while, with the futures of Edson Alvarez and Soungoutou Magassa up in the air. Arne Engels has been the only regular in the midfield, but he needs a partner who can offer a powerful presence alongside him.

Nelson Deossa was targeted by WHUFC in the summer, and he can be the answer to their midfield problems. The Colombian has played sixteen matches so far for Real Betis this season and is under contract until 2030.

Tomas Soucek has served as a key physical asset in midfield, but a long-term heir for his role is needed. Deossa would bring strength, power and work rate, as well as a well-rounded game in possession with regard to his passing and ball carrying.

A January deal could be tough given Deossa’s calibre and the Hammers’ status in the Championship, but it would be an ambitious and exciting move for the club to make.

One of West ham’s defensive issues this season has been at left-back. Nuno favoured Morato in that position while Ollie Scarles has had opportunities and Ezra Mayers is breaking through, but no one has really made that spot their own.

One man who could be an immediate fix is Matt Targett, who starred in the Championship with Middlesbrough last season. The Englishman’s move to Hull City has not worked out and a winter change of scenery could be just what he needs.

WHUFC could land a quick fix at left-back with Targett while youngsters Mayers and Scarles find opportunities as backup and competition.

#2064. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2063. Sheffield Wednesday owner David Storch must watch Josh Windass situation

A new era is underway at Sheffield Wednesday following the appointment of Dave Challinor as the club's new manager.

Wednesday made the decision to part company with Henrik Pedersen last month following an inconsistent start to life back in League One, and Challinor has been tasked with getting their promotion push back on track.

Challinor had been out of work since leaving Stockport County in June after a near five-year spell at Edgeley Park, during which time he led the Hatters from the National League to League One, and his side missed out on promotion to the Championship in his final game as they were beaten by Bolton Wanderers in last season's play-off final.

The 51-year-old, who has also had spells with the likes of AFC Fylde and Hartlepool United, boasts the incredible record of finishing in the play-offs or higher in each of his 15 full seasons as a manager, winning promotion on seven occasions.

Challinor will be looking to add an eighth promotion to his CV with Wednesday this season, but given that the club were forced to operate under transfer restrictions in the summer as the consequences of Dejphon Chansiri's disastrous reign continue to bite, there are question marks over whether the current squad is good enough to secure a return to the Championship.

It is unclear when the remaining constraints on the Owls will be lifted, but once they are able to spend freely, owner David Storch should consider making an ambitious move for one of the club's former fan favourites.

While Storch's takeover marked the start of a bright new era at Hillsborough, Wednesday turned to a few familiar faces this summer as they rebuilt their squad.

Midfielder Barry Bannan achieved club legend status during a 10-and-a-half year spell with the Owls after arriving on a free transfer from Crystal Palace in 2015, but, amid the off-field uncertainty, he departed for Millwall in January.

However, after less than six months at The Den, Bannan made an emotional return to Wednesday in July, and the deal was a clear indication of the fact that Storch and the new hierarchy were keen not to distance themselves too much from the club's past.

Bannan was not the only ex-Owls star to re-join the club this summer, with goalkeeper Joe Lumley and defender Reece James, who was part of the squad that won promotion from League One in the 2022-23 season, also returning for second stints in South Yorkshire.

Of course, Storch should not rely too heavily on sentimental signings, and Bannan's somewhat underwhelming start to the campaign proves that it can be difficult to recapture previous magic, but he should weigh up a swoop for forward Josh Windass if Challinor succeeds in leading Wednesday to promotion this season.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Windass spent five-and-a-half years with Wednesday after joining from Wigan Athletic in January 2020, scoring 53 goals and providing 23 assists in 182 appearances in all competitions, including a 123rd-minute winner in the play-off final against Barnsley at Wembley in 2023 to seal the club's promotion to the Championship.

However, as the scale of the Owls' crisis under Chansiri became clear last summer, Windass opted to terminate his contract at Hillsborough, and he subsequently made the move to Championship newcomers Wrexham.

Windass enjoyed an outstanding debut campaign at the SToK Cae Ras last season, scoring 16 goals and registering seven assists in 46 appearances in all competitions, but it was not enough to help the Red Dragons into the play-offs as they missed out on the top six on the final day.

It has been a frustrating start to the current season for Windass, with the 32-year-old registering just one assist in six appearances during what has been an injury-hit start to the campaign, and his absence has certainly been felt by Phil Parkinson's side.

Given his importance to the team, Wrexham would likely be reluctant to allow Windass to leave next summer, but should Wednesday win promotion to the Championship, there is no doubt that the forward would be an exciting signing to kickstart the next phase of the Storch era.

Windass still regularly references his former club on social media, most recently taking to Instagram to react to the appointment of his ex-Rangers team-mate Clint Hill as Challinor's assistant, which suggests that he does still hold plenty of affection for the Owls and may well be open to a potential return.

Should Sheffield Wednesday bring Josh Windass back to Hillsborough in the future or is it time to move on? Tell us in the comments below!

Whichever division they are in next season, Wednesday will likely have to recruit a new forward line, with many of their existing attackers, including Davis Keillor-Dunn, Harry Gray, Ali Al-Hamadi and Mason Burstow, only on loan, while Jamal Lowe's contract is due to expire at the end of the season.

#2062. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2061. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

Manchester United are reportedly looking at options beyond Michael Carrick after the club believes he is not the right option for United.

Former Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann is among the names linked with a possible move to Old Trafford if United

Indykaila, a famous insider account on X, reported that Manchester United have started the process of finding their next head coach. Nagelsmann’s representatives are said to be willing to hear what the club has planned before deciding whether the project would suit the German manager.

Exclusive 💣Manchester United begin process to identify next head coach, sources indicate.Club sources have confirmed that Manchester United have started formal progress on appointing a new manager.Representatives of Julian Nagelsmann are open to listening to the club’s…

United have not announced any change in their managerial plans, so the report remains unconfirmed. Carrick is still in charge, but his results at the start of the new season have given the club plenty to think about.

Michael Carrick did enough during his interim spell last season to earn the job permanently. After taking over following Ruben Amorim’s departure in January, he won 11 of his 16 matches and guided United to third place in the Premier League, securing Champions League qualification.

That run convinced the club to hand him a two-year contract in May. The new campaign, though, has been a disappointing story so far. United have picked up just six points from their first six league games, their worst start since 1985/86.

Their latest setback came against Tottenham on Saturday. Bryan Mbeumo put United ahead, and Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card left Spurs with ten men, yet Dominic Solanke scored in stoppage time to make it 1-1.

Dropping points in those circumstances will only add to the pressure on Carrick, who needs a response from his players quickly.

Julian Nagelsmann has previously been linked with the Old Trafford job, and the latest report has brought his name back into the conversation. The 39-year-old’s representatives are reportedly open to hearing United’s plans, but there is no confirmed agreement or evidence that formal negotiations have taken place.

Carrick’s achievements last season bought him the permanent role, but the opening weeks of this campaign have left little room for further slip-ups.

#2059. £8m Southampton outcast should be 'incredibly ambitious' Charlton Athletic transfer target

Charlton Athletic have been told to target Southampton’s Tom Fellows as they look to strengthen their squad in the January window.

It has been a crazy season so far for the Addicks, who followed up a brilliant start to the campaign with an 11-game winless run.

However, a 2-1 victory over Sheffield United means the Londoners went into the international break on a high, and whilst they are 17th in the table, they do have a seven-point advantage over the relegation zone.

Nevertheless, it’s clear that Jones’ squad is lacking in certain departments, and the January window will provide an opportunity for the boss to add quality.

However, the January window is notoriously difficult, and with Charlton not working with the biggest budget in the division, they will have to be smart with how they recruit.

And, when asked by FLW about one player the Addicks should try to bring in, Charlton fan pundit Chris Woodward explained why he feels the club should pursue a loan move for Southampton’s Tom Fellows, as he compared it to a previous deal involving James Bree that worked for all parties.

“We haven’t exactly got the budget to splash the cash. I think we’re limited in the quality moves we can make, especially in an inflated window. Therefore, I think we will have to look to the loan market," Chris told FLW.

“One position we lack right now is a natural right winger, and the squad in general is lacking creativity. It’s incredibly ambitious, but I’d look to try and take Tom Fellows on loan, as he ticks both boxes.

“It seems silly to suggest, but 12 months ago we had James Bree on loan, and now he is one of the best full-backs in the league!

“Fellows is out of form and out of favour at Southampton, and he’s not exactly loved by the fans at the moment. So he needs to build his confidence back up and get back to the player he was.

Find out which Championship team takes top spot for the highest house prices around their stadium from 2026 figures.

“Fellows is above Charlton’s level, but he may look at it as a chance to be a key player in a team where he would get a lot of the focus, and Southampton may look at the work we did with Bree, and some of our previous loans, and see how we turned them around. It's an ambitious signing, but it would be an incredible one.”

This may seem like a bold move, but the reality is that Fellows is enduring a difficult period right now, and he is not getting the game time he would’ve wanted a year on from his initial £8 million move from West Brom.

You can understand why Tonda Eckert is playing Kuryu Matsuki, as he is doing very well right now, but Fellows still isn’t getting the minutes he would’ve wanted, as he has been an unused sub in five of the last seven games.

At 23, Fellows is at a stage in his career where he needs to be playing regularly, and Southampton will know that they risk stalling his career if he stays on the bench.

So, if they can bring in a winger during the window themselves, a loan shouldn’t be ruled out for Fellows. And, as mentioned, the way Charlton helped Bree would give them a shot at making this happen if Fellows was available.

Most would agree that Charlton do need attacking additions in January as the lack of creativity and goals was a major problem in their poor run prior to the Blades win.

There was a reliance on Tyreece Campbell earlier in the campaign, and he was always going to struggle to sustain the numbers he was producing at that stage.

As well as his goals, Campbell is one of few players in the squad with genuine pace, so, even if they can’t get Fellows, he is the profile that they need to try and get in January.

Jones and the recruitment team have shown they have an eye for a player over the years, so it will be interesting to see who they do bring in, even if there’s a lot of football to be played before the window opens.

#2057. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

#2056. Tom Cannon in, George Hirst out: How Stoke City's dream January transfer window looks?

Stoke City are dreaming of a return to the Premier League once again after an excellent start to the 2026/27 campaign, and if Mark Robins' side can maintain this level of form for the next couple of months, the January transfer window becomes crucial to their efforts.

Stoke are flying right now in the Championship, sitting level on points with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough in 1st and 2nd, and narrowly ahead of West Bromwich Albion and Wolverhampton Wanderers in 4th and 5th, respectively.

The Potters, after three defeats on the spin to open the season against Swansea City, Southampton, and Wolverhampton, have followed that up with just one defeat in their following 12, winning nine.

If Mark Robins' side can maintain this level of form into the new year, the January window presents an opportunity to go all out and do what they can to secure promotion, as Football League World takes a look at what a dream window in the Potteries may look like.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

Stoke have four different options they could start up front right now, namely George Hirst, Robert Bozenik, Lamine Cisse, and Sam Gallagher, though none of them has really been able to nail down a spot in the starting XI this campaign.

Hirst arrived in the summer from Ipswich Town for a potential £10 million, and with just one goal and one assist in 14 Championship appearances thus far, he failed to justify that fee.

Cisse enjoyed a run of games in the side between mid-September and mid-October, but injury has meant that Bozenik has been preferred up top as of late, whilst Gallagher also recovers from a fresh injury.

Despite this bloated list of strikers, there have been cries for another option up top from Stoke supporters as of late, with Sheffield United's Tom Cannon a name that is well-known in the Potteries.

Cannon, 23, scored 11 times in 25 appearances across all competitions on loan for Stoke from Leicester City during the first half of the 2024/25 campaign, before subsequently joining Sheffield United in January 2025 for around £10 million.

Things have not quite worked out at Bramall Lane for Cannon just yet, and given his popularity at the bet365 Stadium, he would be a dream addition for many supporters; whether a deal is likely, however, is doubtful.

If Cannon were to arrive, it would surely mean that one of their current strike force must depart, and following his lack of impact since his arrival, Hirst would likely be many fans' option to make way.

The former Leicester and Blackburn Rovers striker has never been prolific in his career, hitting double digits in goals in a season just twice at 27, despite earning three promotions with Ipswich under Kieran McKenna.

Whilst it is unlikely Hirst will be going anywhere anytime soon, his failure to justify his hefty fee, as well as Stoke supporters' preference for Cisse, Bozenik, and Gallagher, make him the ideal player to depart.

In reality, one of Bozenik or Gallagher is more likely to leave in January; with the latter's contract due to expire in the summer and now aged 31, it's doubtful he will be offered fresh terms, especially with a subpar injury record.

What would be your dream January window, Stoke fans? Who would you like to see join, and who would you like to see depart? Share your thoughts below!

There are numerous players, as a result of Stoke's summer recruitment, that have been pushed out to the fringes of the squad, as the likes of Bae Jun-ho, Million Manhoef, Tomas Rigo, Ben Pearson, and Ben Gibson have seen their minutes slashed.

Jun-ho, 23, is due to enter the final 12 months of his deal in North Staffordshire, and at this stage, a fresh deal appears incredibly unlikely, as the emergence of Justin Devenny and Jack McGlynn has seen the Korean's game time dwindle.

Ben Pearson has managed just 14 minutes of Championship football this season, with Ethan Galbraith, Djibril Soumare, and Svante Ingelsson's arrivals knocking the midfielder down the pecking order.

Manhoef, Rigo, and Gibson have all barely featured as well, though the most likely to leave in the winter are surely Jun-ho and Pearson, as time will tell how Stoke's season unfolds.

#2055. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

#2052. West Ham can seal £200m jackpot and Sheffield United deal will help them get there

West Ham United are quickly learning that the Championship is no cakewalk. They brought in a promotion specialist, Scott Parker, to help oversee a change in fortunes and a run to the top, but he may need some top-level second-tier players to do so.

The Hammers have a lot of great individuals across the squad, whether that be Jarrod Bowen off the right, a centre-back pairing of Konstantinos Mavropanos and Max Kilman or a promotion-winning duo of Manor Solomon and Joel Piroe in their frontline.

In midfield, though, it's arguable that the current engine room doesn't have the quality to push towards the top two.

Divine Mukasa has been a promising, young, attacking option, but outside of that, record-breaking £22 million arrival Arne Engels hasn't lived up to the hype surrounding that price tag, and Tomas Soucek and Mohamadou Kante have been fine options, but it's not a midfield core with the experience at this level to help bring about promotion.

With the midfield options at the London Stadium, it's no surprise that West Ham were looking to add Sheffield United's Sydie Peck to their ranks following their relegation from the Premier League.

And while the record-breaking deal for Engels wasn't done at the time of these reports, it should still be something that the Hammers reconsider returning to as the January transfer window looms.

Peck had a great year last season, adding some goals to his game, captaining the side at times and being a bright spark in an otherwise dismal campaign for the Blades. This year, though, he's found a new level.

The 22-year-old is starting to influence games further forward under Chris Wilder. He's among the leading defensive midfielders in the division when it comes to creating chances, taking shots and scoring goals.

His hat-trick against Preston North End was an example of what he can do in an attacking sense now, taking his overall goal contributions this season to seven in 17 in all competitions, just three fewer than he managed last year.

Peck's value is arguably as high as it has ever been heading into this January. For a Sheffield United side that is well documented to be struggling financially due to the lack of Premier League parachute payments and the new SCR rules, cashing in could be something the higher-ups decide to do.

Especially given his current contract situation, too, with him entering the final 18 months of his deal. If a new contract can't be hashed out by the end of the year, the Blades face losing out on the amount of profit they could make on the 22-year-old.

We've seen in the past Sheffield United being forced to sell players at a cut-price once they enter the final years of their deals. The likes of Iliman Ndiaye, Anel Ahmedhodzic and, more recently, Gustavo Hamer, all left for less than their perceived market value in their final year.

Peck will be in the final year of his contract come the summer, unless a new deal can be reached. Last month, Blades boss Chris Wilder expressed optimism that these players could be tied down, but with the 22-year-old especially showing Premier League potential, it may be difficult to persuade him to stick around at a Sheffield United side that doesn't seem to be any closer to a top-flight return.

Unfortunately, West Ham weren't the only side to monitor Peck over the summer window. Premier League outfits Nottingham Forest and Brentford were interested, and in a recent report from TEAMtalk, so are now North-East rivals Sunderland and Newcastle United.

The fact that so many top-flight teams are being mentioned alongside the Hammers in their interest in Peck will make it difficult for the London Stadium-based side to strike a deal, as they could offer them Premier League football immediately.

At West Ham, all they can do is promise they'll get there for the start of next season. That could lend well to a deal, as it would allow Peck to progress into the Premier League with a new club, rather than being thrown in at the deep end midway through a season.

Do you think West Ham could beat out Premier League interest in a Sydie Peck pursuit? Let us know in the comments.

But on the flip side, if the Hammers don't secure promotion this year, it'll be another year in the Championship for a midfielder who is destined for the top flight.

The chance to take Peck back down to the capital should also put West Ham ahead of some other suitors, too. The 22-year-old came through at Arsenal before signing for Sheffield United. It may be a stretch, but it could work in their favour.

The Premier League is the most lucrative division in England. Promotion can earn a side £200 million in extra income from TV deals and commercial fees.

It's well-known that the longer a club stays in the Championship, the harder it is to get out of it. The likes of Norwich City, Watford and West Brom have flailed around in this division for a little while now; Sheffield United look to be becoming the next team to.

FLW looks at which of the division's 24 clubs are the biggest and lowest spenders

West Ham cannot afford for that to happen, especially given the size and stature of their club and the ground they play in. No side has a divine right to get promoted, but if the 62.500-capacity London Stadium remains a second-tier ground, that could end up being detrimental to the Hammers' revenue.

Promotion is a must this season, and with Scott Parker at the helm, they'll need to back him as much as they can in the winter transfer window at the turn of the new year. Adding Peck would be a real statement of intent.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2050. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.
